c47_hypothesis.name: Up-Down Quote Volume Imbalance Exhaustion Mean Reversion
c47_hypothesis.description: Split real quote volume by return sign over rolling W=24h: up_vol=sum(qvol|ret>0), down_vol=sum(qvol|ret<0). imbalance=(up_vol-down_vol)/(up_vol+down_vol+eps), z-scored over 168h (causal). Fade exhaustion: imbalance_z>=1.25 and ret_W>0 -> SHORT; imbalance_z<=-1.25 and ret_W<0 -> LONG. Exit on normalization |imb_z|<0.25, max hold 12h, or flip. Execution t->t+1. WF 720/168/168, cost grid 0-40bps, B&H benchmark on same OOS windows.
c47_hypothesis.differs_from_c23: C23 trades high vol_z LEVEL momentum continuation; C47 splits volume into up/down by return sign and fades extreme imbalance ratio with confirming price move.
c47_hypothesis.differs_from_c40: C40 fades HIGH volume climax (aggregate vol_z level); C47 uses directional up/down volume split imbalance, not aggregate volume level climax.
c47_hypothesis.differs_from_c41: C41 continues on LOW vol_z dry-up breakout; C47 mean-reverts on extreme up/down volume imbalance exhaustion.
c47_hypothesis.differs_from_c42: C42 confirms breakouts on volume expansion; C47 uses up/down split imbalance ratio fade, no breakout/expansion confirmation.
c47_hypothesis.differs_from_c43: C43 fades volume-price divergence using unsloped vol_z at price-trend extremes (reversion); C47 uses a rolling up/down volume split imbalance z-score (directional signed-volume partition) with ret_W confirmation — different construction and signal.
c47_hypothesis.differs_from_c44: C44 trend-follows on vol_z ROC acceleration; C47 mean-reverts on extreme up/down volume imbalance ratio, no ROC/acceleration.
c47_hypothesis.differs_from_c45: C45 mean-reverts on Amihud illiquidity SHOCKS (|ret|/volume); C47 uses up/down volume partition imbalance, not price-impact ratio.
c47_hypothesis.differs_from_c46: C46 continues on OBV (cumulative sign*vol) slope divergence vs price slope; C47 uses rolling up/down volume split imbalance ratio z-score with exhaustion fade — different transform (partitioned sums ratio vs cumulative OBV slopes) and opposite mechanic (fade vs continuation).
